FreshHarvest Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the FreshHarvest Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing and using your microphone will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, VP, Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss FreshHarvest Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Growth Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: overall company performance highlights, impact of new product innovations and launches, capital expenditure plans and priorities, and organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year.

First, regarding overall company performance highlights: Good morning, everyone. I'm excited to highlight what was a standout quarter for FreshHarvest Foods amid a resilient yet challenging macro environment in the Food & Beverage sector. Let's dive into the numbers and the drivers behind them.

At the top line, we posted net revenues of $14.2 billion, up 9.2% year-over-year and 4.1% organically, excluding foreign exchange and the divestiture of our low-margin European dairy unit from last year. This extends our streak to the 11th straight quarter of organic top-line growth, surpassing the sector's typical 3-5% as tracked by IRI and Nielsen for the period. Looking through our price/mix/volume framework, price and mix drove 6.8 points from targeted pricing of 7-9% across the board to counter inflation in key commodities—cocoa up 45% YoY, sugar up 22%, and edible oils up 18%. Volumes edged up 0.2%, balancing retailer inventory discipline and some at-home softness with gains in away-from-home channels. Mix contributed another 2.1 points, propelled by premiumization in our Elevate better-for-you snacks and beverages lineup, which expanded 18% organically and grabbed share in the $250 billion global health and wellness space.

Profitability improved sharply, with adjusted gross margins widening 210 basis points to 38.4%—our best in five years—due to our supply chain overhaul launched in 2021. Highlights include the Precision Sourcing platform, powered by AI predictive analytics with IBM Watson, which streamlined procurement for 85% of tropical fruit inputs and generated $450 million in COGS reductions year-to-date. We also secured 70% of next year's wheat and corn at fixed rates through forwards, shielding us from Russia-Ukraine supply ripples that hit peers like Mondelez and Hershey.

This flowed to adjusted operating income of $2.8 billion, up 14.7% with margins up 140 basis points to 19.7%. SG&A deleveraged 60 basis points to 11.2% of sales via zero-based budgeting and the Fit for Growth program, which cut indirect headcount by 15% while funding high-return digital tools like SAP S/4HANA for demand sensing. Adjusted diluted EPS hit $1.68, a 15.8% increase and 8% ahead of our guidance midpoint, underscoring earnings quality.

Free cash flow came in strong at $1.9 billion, up 22% YoY, funding $1.2 billion in share repurchases from our $10 billion program and a 12% dividend increase to $0.52 per share next month. The balance sheet is rock-solid: net leverage at 2.1x EBITDA, $8.5 billion in liquidity, and investment-grade ratings from S&P and Moody's.

By segment, our portfolio shone through. Beverages, 45% of revenues, grew 7.5% organically to $6.4 billion, with core carbonated soft drinks flat at +2% volume amid headwinds but boosted by non-carb functionals like HydraBoost electrolytes, up 25% and gaining 1.2 share points versus Gatorade per Nielsen. Snacks & Confectionery, 35% of the mix, jumped 12.1% to $5.0 billion—chocolate volumes steady at +1% despite cocoa swings, savory snacks like CrunchVita baked chips riding 15% health-snack growth. Nutrition & Wellness, 20% of revenues and our top performer, rose 14.3% organically to $2.8 billion, led by plant-based proteins such as GreenFuel pea-protein bars up 28%, in line with McKinsey's 20%+ CAGR for alt-proteins to 2027.

Geographically, strength was widespread. North America, 55% of sales, grew 8.9% organically, lifted by e-commerce at 18% penetration via Amazon and Instacart partnerships, plus 10% foodservice rebound post-Omicron. EMEA advanced 6.2% in constant currency, managing energy costs with local pricing and 80% recyclable beverage packaging ahead of EU plastics rules. Asia-Pacific, 20% of revenues, surged 15.4% on China premium snacks up 22% and India functionals via Reliance Retail. Latin America grew 11.7%, with Brazil volumes +5% on real pricing and Mexico nearshoring trimming logistics 12%.

These outcomes reinforce our Taste the Future strategy: innovation, portfolio shaping, and sustainability. We've introduced 22 SKUs this year, with 35 more in the pipeline, including ReVive snack bars from upcycled spent grain with AB InBev partners. M&A is selective; the $1.2 billion VitaPure collagen acquisition adds 200 bps to FY24 EPS. ESG progress includes 18% Scope 3 emissions cuts via regenerative ag on 40% of cocoa farms with Barry Callebaut, outpacing Unilever in consumer polls.

In short, Q3 had us performing across growth, margins, and cash in a 12-15% inflation year per FMI. We're lifting FY24 guidance to 8-9% organic revenue growth, adjusted EPS of $6.45-$6.55, and free cash flow over 95% of EBITDA.

Second, concerning the impact of new product innovations and launches: Before moving on, let me highlight a major driver of our outperformance: our new product innovations and launches. In Food & Beverage, new product development is essential for growth as consumers chase health, sustainability, and convenience.

The proof is in the results. Innovations from the last 12 months generated $285 million in incremental net revenue in Q3—up 142% YoY—and accounted for 18% of our $1.58 billion quarterly revenue from those channels, versus 9% last year. On a two-year basis, velocity is +27%, beating category norms by 15 points per Nielsen, with gross margins at 48.2%, 320 bps above average, from better formulations and supply chains.

Key launches include VitaGlow Functional Waters, entering the RTD functional space like Celsius and Prime. Launched in February with nootropic citrus for brain boost, collagen berry for skin, and zero-cal electrolytes with adaptogens, it addressed the $12 billion U.S. market at 11% CAGR per Euromonitor. Q3 sales reached $112 million, hitting 62% ACV in North America, ranking #3 behind PepsiCo's Gatorade Fit and Propel, with 28% trial among 18-34s per IRI. Margins at 51% thanks to micro-encapsulation stabilizing ashwagandha sans preservatives.

Next, EarthPure Plant-Based Dairy Alternatives: oat-almond blends using 50% less water than Oatly, with regenerative sourcing. Targeted the $28 billion plant milk market, posting $92 million in Q3 sales, +35% household penetration in UK/Australia. In China via Alibaba Tmall, +210% QoQ versus Mengniu imports amid millennial veganism. LCA shows 40% lower carbon, securing $50 million green financing.

In snacks, KetoCrunch Protein Bars: low-carb, 15g protein, countering GLP-1 appetite suppression in a -4% chocolate category per IRI. $81 million sales, 2.5x Clif Bar velocity, 22% repeat in convenience via precision fermentation mimicking whey allergen-free.

By region: North America (52% of innovation sales) saw +18% lift in Costco/Walmart pilots. EMEA +165% on EU Green Deal tailwinds, APAC +220% in Indonesia/India with local flavors, LATAM +95% despite Brazil FX, with tequila VitaGlow eyeing Mexico #1.

This stems from $180 million R&D over two years—12% of sales above Nestlé's benchmark—including Singapore AI flavor lab cutting cycles to 9 months, IBM Food Trust blockchain, and HPP for 95% bioactive retention.

Ahead, 27 SKUs for 2025 like fermented dairy-free cheese and upcycled bars tap $65 billion opportunity per Bain, at +25% price premium for 20-22% CAGR, gaining 110 bps share per Kantar versus PepsiCo and Danone.

Innovation bolsters top-line, margins, and resilience in our $4.5 trillion industry.

Third, in terms of capital expenditure plans and priorities: As we look ahead, our capital expenditure outlook is central to sustainable growth, efficiency, and market share in Food & Beverage. For fiscal 2024, we expect $650 million in CapEx, up 12% from $580 million in FY2023. This measured increase supports mid-teens EBITDA growth while targeting 14-16% ROIC on new spends—above our WACC.

Priorities align with capacity expansion in high-margin areas, supply chain resilience, and digital transformation. Allocation: 45% or $290 million to manufacturing/capacity, 25% or $165 million to supply chain/logistics, 20% or $130 million to tech/innovation, 10% to maintenance/sustainability.

Capacity expansion leads with investments in aseptic processing and high-speed filling for plant-based and functional beverages, up 22% YoY in Q3 to 18% of segment sales. Key is our $120 million Midwest greenfield plant, 250,000 sq ft near dairy-alternative hubs for Beyond Meat/Oatly partners, adding 30% capacity for almond/oat milks at 40,000 cases/hour via homogenization. First production Q2 2025, payback under 3 years at 28-30% margins.

In snacks/ready-to-eat, $85 million for three brownfield sites in Texas/Georgia with robotic palletizing and vision systems like PepsiCo's to fight labor shortages, lifting throughput 25% and cutting conversion costs 8-10%.

Regionally: North America (55%, $355 million) on premiumization like low-sugar waters with micro-filtration for zero-additive claims. APAC (20%, $130 million) for protein bars in Indonesia/Vietnam at 15% CAGR per Nielsen. Europe (15%, $100 million) $40 million sustainable packaging for EU plastics directives like Nestlé's 2025 recyclables goal. LATAM on logistics vs. 40% cocoa/coffee spikes.

Supply chain resilience: $165 million includes $60 million for three U.S. Southeast cold-chain DCs with AS/RS and IoT for 99.9% accuracy, cutting stockouts 15% like Keurig Dr Pepper. $50 million onshoring pea protein in Canada vs. 25% Chinese cost hikes.

Tech/innovation: $130 million with $45 million AI predictive maintenance at 15 plants via Rockwell, reducing downtime 20-25% from 85% utilization. $40 million FlavorForge lab in California for clean-label emulsions, eyeing 5% margin gain. All projects feature energy chillers/water recycling for 20% Scope 1 cuts by 2026 like Danone.

These de-risk 8-10% organic growth, boost FCF to 95%+ EBITDA. Stress-tested for 10% inflation, yielding 18% returns even at $7/bushel wheat. FY2025 CapEx at $680 million, tilted digital/sustainability.

This CapEx positions us ahead of Mondelez in snacking ROIC and Kellogg in plant-based.

Finally, looking at organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year: As we shift to forward-looking items, our organic sales growth outlook for Q4 fiscal 2024 is 4% to 6%, gaining from Q3's 5.2%, and 5% to 7% for full FY2025. This balances pricing, volume rebound, and premium mix in Snacks, Beverages, and Convenience Foods.

Pricing tailwind moderates to 2-3% in Q4 from 4.1% Q3 as CPI food-at-home slows to 1.5% YoY per BLS, backed by promotions on HarvestCrunch bars and ZeroWave waters for 3-5% Nielsen velocity in club channels.

Volumes flat to +2% in Q4 from -0.5% Q3, driven by GreenHarvest alt-dairy to 15% Refrigerated sales in $12B U.S. market at 8% CAGR per Euromonitor, and NeuroBoost nootropic waters projecting 20% outperformance like PepsiCo Rockstar.

Mix adds 1-2 points via premium Artisan snacks at 20%+ margins post 12% SKU pruning, lifting ASP 5%.

By region: North America (55% sales) 5-7% Q4 on 110 bps salty snack share per IRI, e-comm at 18%. EMEA 3-5% with plant-based Ocado wins. APAC 8-10% on 15% bev volume like Coke Thums Up. LATAM 6-8% on Brazil convenience.

Technical supports: $250M supply chain across 15 plants hedges cocoa/palm at mid-single inflation via futures; 100% recyclable packaging Q2 FY25 for EU PPWR and Gen Z (65% eco per Kantar).

Risks hedged by 70/30 domestic/international mix vs. FX/tariffs; tailwinds in 6% premium snacking, 10%+ functional hydration. Conservative volumes but upside vs. Kellogg/Monster.

FY25's 5-7% sets compounding EPS. 

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. As Mike outlined, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $14.2 billion, representing a 9.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.4%, bolstered by supply chain efficiencies. Operating income was $2.8 billion, and earnings per share were $1.68. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $8.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance for 8-9% organic revenue growth, adjusted EPS of $6.45 to $6.55.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Good question, John. As Mike noted earlier, we've navigated inflation effectively with pricing actions averaging 7-9% to offset rises in cocoa up 45%, sugar 22%, and oils 18%. Our Precision Sourcing AI and forward contracts have locked in key inputs, delivering $450 million COGS savings YTD and margin expansion. We're positioned well as CPI eases.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new products like VitaGlow and what is the expected impact?

Raj Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. VitaGlow functional waters have been a standout, generating $112 million in Q3 with 62% ACV and #3 U.S. ranking, at 51% margins. Expect continued 20%+ category outperformance, contributing 1-2 points to mix shift in FY25 guidance, alongside pipeline like fermented cheeses for sustained innovation velocity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Ramirez (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Great question, Mike. We're investing $165 million in resilience, including three Southeast cold-chain DCs with AS/RS and IoT for 99.9% accuracy, cutting stockouts 15%, plus onshoring pea protein. Combined with $250 million program hedging 80% FY25 inputs, we've de-risked volatility and support volume recovery.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Laura Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Laura Kim (Morgan Stanley):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Laura, our raised FY24 guidance embeds 8-9% organic growth and $6.45-6.55 EPS, with Q4 at 4-6%. FY25 at 5-7% builds on pricing discipline, volume tailwinds, and mix from innovations. Conservative but with upside from share gains and CapEx ROIC.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in FreshHarvest Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
